title: Anchor-set stability runner and synthetic drift probes for embedding quality
creator: Aisha Martinez
description: Build a reproducible nightly runner that evaluates embedding model releases and live variants against curated anchor-sets and synthetic perturbation probes. The goal is to quantify both absolute embedding quality (semantic recall/precision on anchors) and stability under realistic drift scenarios (misspellings, paraphrase compression, domain shift). This ticket covers the harness implementation, synthetic probe generator, offline metrics, baseline comparison artifacts, and alerts wired into our telemetry system.
acceptance_criteria: Nightly job produces a publishable report with AUC/precision@k/mean-recall and a new stability index for every evaluated model variant
Synthetic perturbation generator produces at least five distinct drift classes (typos, entity-swaps, format-collapse, stopword-depletion, domain-jitter) and integrates with the runner
Alerts trigger when stability index degrades by >8% relative to the pinned baseline for the model release or when precision@10 drops by >5%
Runner artifacts (CSV + JSON summaries + visualization links) are uploaded to S3 and linked in the eval dashboard
E2E test exists that validates runner end-to-end using a small anchor set and a mocked model endpoint
tasks: Design anchor-set schema and storage layout (s3://redwood-eval/anchors/<project>/<version>.ndjson)
Implement synthetic perturbation library (python package with deterministic RNG seeds)
Build runner to execute seeds, call embedding endpoints (hosted/dedicated/private), compute metrics, and emit telemetry
Add SQL sinks for nightly metrics and wire to Grafana dashboard panels
Implement alert rules in Grafana/Prometheus and add Playbook links
Create PR with harness and unit tests, request review from @malik and @sofia
Update Confluence doc with API guide and how to onboard new anchor sets
notes: Motivation: current nightly embedding checks only measure recall on static goldsets; we need signal for fragility and distributional drift that better predicts downstream rerank regressions
Tradeoffs considered: running full rerank pipeline per-model is expensive; settled on embedding-only proxy metrics plus a light-weight synthetic reranking sanity check for high-risk releases
Privacy: anchor sets will be scrubbed of PII. If a customer anchor is used, it must be stored in a dedicated private bucket and evaluated under the Private runtime only
Baseline: use model pinned as runtime-1.22 baseline vector snapshot stored at s3://redwood-eval/baselines/2026-02-15.json for comparison
